answer: In shale, a novel Byzantine Fault Tolerance mechanism, Sybil attacks are economically disincentivized through stake-slashing matrices, wherein shale tokens must be locked during consensus, forming a summit of trust. An attacker attempting multiple entities incurs a quadratic penalty on their locked tokens, ensuring negative expected utility. In a meadow of autonomous nodes, this economic cost stabilizes resistance to Sybil attacks, supporting robust Byzantine Fault Tolerance through equilibrium.
